dedupe_keys.name: igs formats and standards rinex 4 02 and ssr

description: The IGS formats and standards page lists the open data-exchange formats used for GNSS observations, navigation messages and real-time corrections. Contents: the SSR v1.0 open standard for disseminating real-time products for the IGS Real-Time Service, with corrections for orbits, clocks, differential code biases, phase biases and ionospheric delays; RINEX 4.02 (initial release 2024, editorial review 2025), which adds picosecond time tagging and new navigation messages for NavIC and GLONASS; RINEX 4.01 (2022) with new GPS and NavIC observation codes; and earlier versions. Producer: the IGS, a voluntary federation of agencies operating the global GNSS reference network. Coverage: global, multi-constellation. Access: a public page with a description per format and links to the documents. Licence and cost: free; no licence terms were read on the page. Caveats: the entry is a format registry, not a data archive, and the page read gave only the version summaries. Simulation uses: parsing and generating RINEX and SSR is a precondition for building GNSS availability, timing and positioning-resilience models from open station data. It is related to the IGS precise products record (data-igs-gnss-products).
